questions.stem:
A disease is known to be present in 2% of a population. A test is developed to help determine whether or not someone has the disease.

Given that a person has the disease, the test is positive with probability 0.95

Given that a person does not have the disease, the test is positive with probability 0.03

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw a tree diagram to represent this information.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: Tree without probabilities or labels. A1: 0.02(Disease), 0.95(Positive) on correct branches. A1: 0.03(Positive) on correct branch.
Notes: M1: All 6 branches. Bracketed probabilities not required.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
A person is selected at random from the population and tested for this disease.
(b) Find the probability that the test is positive.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\mathrm{P(Positive Test)} = 0.02\times 0.95 + 0.98\times 0.03$ M1A1ft $= 0.0484$ A1
Notes: M1 for sum of two products, at least one correct from their diagram. A1ft follows from the probabilities on their tree. A1 for correct answer only or $\frac{121}{2500}$.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
A doctor randomly selects a person from the population and tests him for the disease. Given that the test is positive,
(c) find the probability that he does not have the disease.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\mathrm{P(Do\ not\ have\ disease | Positive\ test)} = \frac{0.98\times 0.03}{0.0484}$ M1 $= 0.607438..$ awrt 0.607 A1
Notes: M1 for conditional probability with numerator following from their tree and denominator their answer to part (b). A1 also for $\frac{147}{242}$.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Comment on the usefulness of this test.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (d) Test not very useful OR High probability of not having the disease for a person with a positive test B1

questions.stem:
A person's blood group is determined by whether or not it contains any of 3 substances $A$, $B$ and $C$.

A doctor surveyed 300 patients' blood and produced the table below.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline \text{Blood contains} & \text{No. of Patients}\\ \hline \text{only } C & 100\\ \hline A \text{ and } C \text{ but not } B & 100\\ \hline \text{only } A & 30\\ \hline B \text{ and } C \text{ but not } A & 25\\ \hline \text{only } B & 12\\ \hline A, B \text{ and } C & 10\\ \hline A \text{ and } B \text{ but not } C & 3\\ \hline\end{array}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw a Venn diagram to represent this information.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) M1: 3 closed intersecting curves with labels. A1: 100 100, 30. A1: 12, 10, 3, 25. B1: Box.
Notes: 20 not required. Fractions and exact equivalent decimals or percentages.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the probability that a randomly chosen patient's blood contains substance $C$.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\mathrm{P(Substance\ }C) = \frac{100+100+10+25}{300} = \frac{235}{300} = \frac{47}{60}$ or exact equivalent M1A1ft
Notes: M1 For adding their positive values in $C$ and finding a probability. A1ft for correct answer or answer from their working.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Harry is one of the patients. Given that his blood contains substance $A$,
(c) find the probability that his blood contains all 3 substances.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\mathrm{P(All\ 3\,|\,}A) = \frac{10}{30+3+10+100} = \frac{10}{143}$ or exact equivalent M1A1ft
Notes: M1 their 10 divided by their sum of values in $A$. A1ft for correct answer or answer from their working.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
Patients whose blood contains none of these substances are called universal blood donors.
(d) Find the probability that a randomly chosen patient is a universal blood donor.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) $\mathrm{P(Universal\ donor)} = \frac{20}{300} = \frac{1}{15}$ or exact equivalent M1A1 cao
Notes: M1 for 'their 20' divided by 300. A1 correct answer only.

questions.stem:
The discrete random variable $X$ can take only the values 2, 3 or 4. For these values the cumulative distribution function is defined by

$\mathrm{F}(x) = \frac{(x+k)^2}{25}$ for $x=2,3,4$

where $k$ is a positive integer.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $\mathrm{F}(4)=1$. $(4+k)^2=25$ M1. $k=1$ as $k>0$ A1
Notes: M1 for use of $\mathrm{F}(4)=1$ only if $\mathrm{F}(2)=1$ and/or $\mathrm{F}(3)=1$ seen then M0. $\mathrm{F}(2)+\mathrm{F}(3)+\mathrm{F}(4)=1$ M0. A1 for $k=1$ and ignore $k=-9$.

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 2 & 3 & 4\\ \hline \mathrm{P}(X=x) & \frac{9}{25} & \frac{7}{25} & \frac{9}{25}\\ \hline\end{array}$ B1ftB1B1
Notes: B1ft follow through their $k$ for $\mathrm{P}(X=2)$ either exact or 3sf between 0 and 1 inclusive. B1 correct answer only or exact equivalent. B1 correct answer only or exact equivalent.

questions.question_text:
The discrete random variable $X$ can take only the values 2, 3 or 4. For these values the cumulative distribution function is defined by

$\mathrm{F}(x) = \frac{(x+k)^2}{25}$ for $x=2,3,4$

where $k$ is a positive integer.
(a) Find $k$.
(2)
(b) Find the probability distribution of $X$.
(3)
questions.mark_scheme_text:
(a) $\mathrm{F}(4)=1$. $(4+k)^2=25$ M1. $k=1$ as $k>0$ A1
Notes: M1 for use of $\mathrm{F}(4)=1$ only if $\mathrm{F}(2)=1$ and/or $\mathrm{F}(3)=1$ seen then M0. $\mathrm{F}(2)+\mathrm{F}(3)+\mathrm{F}(4)=1$ M0. A1 for $k=1$ and ignore $k=-9$.
(b) $\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline x & 2 & 3 & 4\\ \hline \mathrm{P}(X=x) & \frac{9}{25} & \frac{7}{25} & \frac{9}{25}\\ \hline\end{array}$ B1ftB1B1
Notes: B1ft follow through their $k$ for $\mathrm{P}(X=2)$ either exact or 3sf between 0 and 1 inclusive. B1 correct answer only or exact equivalent. B1 correct answer only or exact equivalent.

questions.stem: A packing plant fills bags with cement. The weight $X$ kg of a bag of cement can be modelled by a normal distribution with mean 50 kg and standard deviation 2 kg.

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) $z=\frac{53-50}{2}$ Attempt to standardise M1. $\mathrm{P}(X>53)=1-\mathrm{P}(Z<1.5)$ 1-probability required can be implied B1. $=1-0.9332$ $=0.0668$ A1
Notes: (a) M1 for using 53, 50 and 2, either way around on numerator. B1 1- any probability for mark. A1 0.0668 cao

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the weight that is exceeded by 99% of the bags.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\mathrm{P}(X\leqslant x_0)=0.01$ M1. $\frac{x_0-50}{2}=-2.3263$ M1B1. $x_0=45.3474$ awrt 45.3 or 45.4 M1A1
Notes: (b) M1 can be implied or seen in a diagram or equivalent with correct use of 0.01 or 0.99. M1 for attempt to standardise with 50 and 2 numerator either way around. B1 for $\pm 2.3263$. M1 Equate expression with 50 and 2 to a $z$ value to form an equation with consistent signs and attempt to solve. A1 awrt 45.3 or 45.4

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Three bags are selected at random.
(c) Find the probability that two weigh more than 53 kg and one weighs less than 53 kg.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\mathrm{P(2\ weigh\ more\ than\ 53kg\ and\ 1\ less)} = 3\times 0.0668^2(1-0.0668)$ B1M1A1ft $=0.012492487..$ awrt 0.012 A1
Notes: (c) B1 for 3. M1 $p^2(1-p)$ for any value of $p$. A1ft for $p$ is their answer to part (a) without 3. A1 awrt 0.012 or 0.0125
